In circular motion, velocity changes at every point along the path, but the speed remains
constant throughout the motion. (While varying velocity with constant speed is
possible, the scenario of varying speed with constant acceleration is not achievable.)
Velocity –Time Graph
A velocity-time graph is a visual representation that illustrates a journey.
For the graph, we take velocity in Y- axis and the time in X – axis. A velocity-time graph tells
us how someone/something’s velocity has changed over a period of time.

Fig3.3h: the v-t plot for different velocities. In the first section of the plot, there is a slow change in velocity even for a large value of time, hence the body is said to be accelerating slowly. In the second part, there is a rapid increase in velocity over time, signifying quick acceleration. In the third section, there is no change in velocity over time, signifying a steady speed. In the final section, there is a rapid decrease in velocity, representing rapid deceleration that finally returns to its initial state and remains stopped over some interval of time. The body finally speeds up in the opposite direction for a time and remains in a state of steady speed then.

Salient Features: (1) Since the slope of the velocity vs. time (v-t) graph at every point represents acceleration, the graph must be continuous and single-valued to be differentiable. (2) Time always increases, so the graph should never trend in the opposite direction of the time axis. (3) The displacement in a given time interval can be found by calculating the area under the curve between two specified time values. It's crucial that the graph is numerically integrable, meaning it should not have singularities. (4) The graph should never become parallel to v -axis. (5) The velocity-time (v-t) graph for motion with uniformly increasing velocity is a straight line with a positive slope, while for motion with uniformly decreasing velocity, it is a straight line with a negative slope. (6) The velocity-time (v-t) graph of a body with increasing/decreasing acceleration is a curve that exhibits a continuously increasing/decreasing slope as time progresses.
